content.text:
I'm mapping out the grid row by row to identify which cells belong to the 8-shaped container versus the 9s inside it, so I can erase anything outside the boundary and keep the outline intact.

The tricky part is the vertical line of 9s at column 10 crossing several rows — I need to decide which ones are part of the interior versus stray marks outside the container, and where the outline might need patching where that line breaks through the border.

I'm restoring the outline while keeping the intruding parts only inside the boundary region spanning rows 3-8, columns 3-9. I'm checking whether the vertical lines at column 5 and column 6 that extend from outside into this region are actually the same object, since one runs rows 0-2 and the other rows 9-11 with segments poking inside.

So I'm settling on filling the whole inside segment: border restored fully around the shape, with 2s placed at column 5 rows 3-8, column 6 rows 3-8, and row 6 across columns 3-9, even though it's a bit ambiguous which lines connect.
